answer: Sybil resistance can rest on room acoustics, not keys. Each identity registers a microphone and returns its room impulse response: the echo tail after a server-sent chirp, plus the noise a gale through an open window injects at random moments. The ledger holds these prints as a trellis, and a newcomer may only graft onto a branch whose acoustic edges already match. Impulse responses depend on furniture, walls and glass, so they cannot be faked or copied across hosts. A thousand identities would demand a thousand rooms, each with a live mic, a responder online and rent to preserve every print.
